titulo: Query with impressions and no page: validated topic
lead: A paid tool estimates what people search for. Your Search Console shows what they already searched for and where you appeared. A non-branded query with impressions and no page made for it is a validated topic, for free. In this lesson you sort topics, pages to improve and noise, and you write the brief with a real asset.
objetivo: turn non-branded queries with impressions and no owner page into a topic list of 5 pages, each backed by a real asset.

aprende.t: What an owner page for a query is
Why each topic needs a real asset
The brief for a new page

hero_alt: A hand pins blank paper cards to a corkboard, next to a notebook.

nos.detalhe: The non-branded file from lesson 2 (or the Queries tab of the dashboard, with the filter "does not match" the brand). Each row: query, page, impressions, position.
The same query can show up with two pages. Add up the impressions and keep the best position.
The owner page is the one made for that query: it appears on the first page of Google for it, or it deals with exactly that subject. If there is none, the query has no home.
People searched, and you showed up by chance with another page. Write the page made for that search, if you have a real asset to back it.
The right page already exists, but it sits beyond the first page. Don't write another one: strengthen this one (new sections, internal links, links back to it).

secoes.legenda: Two pages for the same search compete with each other. Before writing, ask whether the owner page already exists.

texto: Keep the non-branded queries that have impressions and make sense for your business.
A search that has nothing to do with you (a typo, a stray name) is noise: ignore it.
For each query, look for the owner page on your site.
No owner: topic. Owner outside the top: improve the owner page.

exemplo.texto: The non-branded queries that appeared the most were in Spanish: "aprender ia" (10 impressions), "aprender inteligencia artificial desde cero" (10), "cómo aprender ia" (8). All landed on the Spanish page about learning AI, between positions 29 and 61. They already had an owner page: the case is to improve, not to write another one.

texto: Every new page rests on a real asset: a course, a project, an experiment, data from your business. Without an asset, the topic waits.
That is what keeps the page from being just another copy of the rest.
A person approves the list before anything is written. At most 5 pages at a time.
No 5 variations of the same keyword: that is content at scale, and Google treats it as spam.

secoes.titulo: Practice: five topics with an asset
secoes.sub: Use the most recent week of your export.

exercicios.texto: Take the 15 non-branded queries with the most impressions and sort each one into topic, improve, or ignore.
exercicios.pronto: the list has 15 rows with impressions, best position, owner page (or "none"), and decision.

exercicios.texto: Pick the strongest topic that has a real asset and fill in the brief.
exercicios.pronto: the brief has a query, intent, a named own data point (a course, a project, or a number of yours), and 2 older pages that will link to the new one.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: A non-branded query has impressions and lands on a page of yours at position 45, built for that subject. Topic or improve?
opcoes: Improve: the owner page exists, it is just far from the top.
perguntas.explica: Writing a second page for the same search makes the two compete. Strengthen the owner page.

perguntas.p: You found a good topic, but you have no course, project, or data of your own on the subject. What do you do?
opcoes: Write it anyway, with generic text.
Leave the topic waiting until you have a real asset.
perguntas.explica: The method only publishes a page backed by a real asset. That is what sets it apart from the others.

perguntas.p: Why not publish 5 variations of the same keyword?
opcoes: Because it is a lot of work.
Because it is content at scale: Google treats it as spam, and the pages compete with each other.
Because Search Console doesn't allow it.
perguntas.explica: Scaled content abuse. And remember the case from lesson 3: a batch of similar pages did not make it into the index.

perguntas.p: Where does the "validated" topic in this lesson come from?
opcoes: From a volume estimate from a paid tool.
From the real queries your site has already appeared for in Search Console.
perguntas.explica: Validated because someone has already searched for it and you have already shown up. The exact search volume isn't available for free; this is.

itens.texto: If the owner page exists, improve it. If it doesn't, it goes on the topic list.
Without a course, project, or data of your own, the topic waits.
Google's guide for AI (May/2026) asks for non-commodity content: your own data and direct experience. It's the same filter as the real asset.
